column5:
(article 17-13 from Wage Tax Act)

  1. A special/extra payment for a period covering several normal pay periods shall be taxed separately.
  2. The tax on the special payment referred to in the first paragraph (in Dutch: bijzondere beloning) can be calculated as follows:
    1. the amount of the special payment is divided by the number of normal wage periods to which the special payment is attributable and then added to the wages charged according to the table over the wage period in which the special payment is received;
    2. on the wage amount obtained as a result under a., the tax is determined according to the periodic wage tax table;
    3. the tax amount as outcome of letter b. is reduced by the amount of tax payable according to the tax table over the normal/periodic salary;
    4. the tax due on the special payment is equal to the outcome of the difference calculated under c multiplied by the number of normal wage periods referred to under a;
    5. the number of wage periods to which the special payment is attributable is equal to the number of wage periods to which the special payment relates.

​​​​​​​The normal tax tariffs apply.

• Description: This wage component represents the employer's contribution towards the pension fund (APF) as required by Suriname's General Pension Law of 2014.Taxability: The employer's contribution is subject to tax.
  • Minimum Salary Basis: The premium is calculated based on a minimum salary base of SRD 500 per month, regardless of the employee’s actual salary.
  • Maximum Salary Basis: The premium is calculated based on a maximum salary base of SRD 5,000 per month. If the employee earns more than SRD 5,000, the calculation will still be based on SRD 5,000.
  • Rate Increase: The total pension premium starts at 3.0% of the gross salary in 2015 and increases annually by 0.5% until it reaches 28% in 2065. The employer's contribution will increase proportionally along with the total premium.
